newsitem.title: RUSSIA: C.bank sells roubles, demand high after Yeltsin op.
newsitem.headline: C.bank sells roubles, demand high after Yeltsin op.

text.p: Rouble demand rose ahead of the long weekend, as government securities looked more attractive after President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery, and dealers said the central bank was selling roubles to limit fluctuations.
Dealers said the central bank was selling dollars for today settlement to saturate the market. No comment from the central bank was available.
November 7 and 8 are holidays in Russia, marking the 1917 Bolshevik revolution, and Sunday will be a working day.
Dealers said investor interest in Russian securities would pick up now that Yeltin has resumed his presidential powers after his quintuple bypass operation.
"T-bill demand is higher, investors could decide to take a risk and invest in T-bills," Moscow Business World bank dealer Alexei Zolotaryov said.

Aljba Alliance bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said banks were seeking roubles ahead of the long weekend. He added roubles were scarce also because today's government bond auctions had dried up the market.
The central bank auctioned eight trillion roubles of six-month GKO T-bills and 2.5 trillion roubles of an additional tranche of OFZ bonds.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,462-65 per dollar compared with an early 5,456-58 and 5,463-65 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles edged down to 5,473-76 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,466-69.
The central bank said it had set 5,464/5,476 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 10-20 percent compared with Tuesday's late 40-60 percent.
